THE COMPLETE DOCTOR ACADEMYMRCPsych Paper B · Domain 13 Research Methods, Statistics, Critical Review and Evidence-Based Practice

Aim and objectives

Aim. To prepare you to critically appraise randomised and other therapy trials and calculate their measures of effect for MRCPsych Paper B.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Explain how randomisation and allocation concealment protect against selection bias, and distinguish concealment from blinding.
  2. Apply intention-to-treat analysis and compare it with per-protocol analysis in handling dropouts and non-adherence.
  3. Calculate relative risk, relative risk reduction, absolute risk reduction and number needed to treat (1/ARR) from a 2x2 table.
  4. Appraise a trial report for subgroup analyses, surrogate outcomes and early stopping, using the CONSORT statement.
  5. Describe n-of-1 and cluster randomised trials, and explain why clustering requires a larger sample size.
  6. Distinguish internal from external validity and explain why sample size reduces random error but not bias.
  7. Answer the chapter's 48 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
